He charged straight in, at a speed impossible for such an imposing mass, crossing the space between himself and the dragon in a barely perceptible fraction of a second. Rex Aira reacted instinctively, spreading its wings in a brutal movement, generating gusts so violent that the air itself seemed to tear around them, translucent cracks streaking through reality with every beat, the white stone of the ground cracking under the pressure of the supernatural wind. Nothing stopped 81. He went through the gusts as if they were nothing but a light breeze, his fist crashing into the dragon's flank with a dull, staggering thud that made the whole creature reel despite its titanic mass. Rex Aira let out a roar of pain, trying to recover, to generate an even more powerful gust — but 81 was already on it, a second blow landing on its jaw, then a third against its ribs, every impact echoing like a thunderclap across the silent expanse. The dragon tried to retreat into the air, its wings beating frantically, but 81 literally leapt after it, grabbing hold of one of its legs before slamming it back down to the ground with a deafening crash, the white stone splitting under the impact into a spiderweb of crevasses. — You can't— Rex Aira tried, its voice trembling, broken with pain, you can't already be this strong, it's impossible, you were sealed, you— — I had all the time in the world to train, 81 cut in, his fist coming down again, without the slightest trace of pity in his voice. Isidora, standing back with Takeshi and Agent 47, watched the scene with a mixture of fascination and obvious caution, instinctively taking another step back with every impact. — Okay, she said softly, almost to herself. Okay, okay, okay. I'd forgotten how freaky it is to watch him fight for real. Takeshi stood frozen, unable to tear his eyes away from the methodical massacre unfolding before him, a chilling certainty slowly settling in him that he had literally just freed something that even the most powerful entities in the universe had deemed necessary to lock away. Isidora, a delighted smile lighting up her face, hurriedly pulled out her phone, the screen lighting up instantly — signal, at last, was back. — Ah, finally! she exclaimed, raising the phone to film the scene. I thought I was going to die without being able to post this. She carefully framed 81 methodically crushing Rex Aira against the cracked white stone, quickly tapping the screen to add a caption. — "My buddy just got out of prison and he's already wrecking an ancient dragon, just another day," she murmured as she typed, a satisfied smile on her lips. #GodKiller #Comeback #Sanctuary Takeshi, still frozen by the horror of the fight, turned his head toward her, incredulous. — You're filming this for Instagram? Here, right now? — Well, yeah, she answered without taking her eyes off the screen, adjusting the angle for a better shot. It's not every day you get to see a dragon massacre live. Gotta immortalize it. A particularly violent roar rang out, Rex Aira making one last attempt to break free, unleashing a gust powerful enough to make Isidora stagger — who, without even panicking, simply steadied her phone with one hand while backing up with the other. — Oh, gorgeous shot, that one, on top of it, she remarked, delighted, before turning her attention back to the fight. Go on, 81, one last hit for the camera! 81, without turning around, without even seeming aware he was being filmed, closed his massive hand around the dragon's neck, lifting it partly off the ground with a gesture of inhuman strength. — You're going to pay, he said in a low voice, for every second I spent locked up. Agent 47, who had stayed silent and perfectly still since the fight began, exchanged a neutral look with Takeshi, as if to underline, without a word, the quiet absurdity of the scene — an ancient cosmic massacre, filmed live for social media by a witch of the Void. 81 slowly raised a single finger, his massive nail extending toward Rex Aira's gargantuan eye, held immobile by the relentless grip crushing its throat. The dragon, unable to break free, let out a strangled cry, its reptilian pupil contracting in pure terror at this tiny, almost trivial gesture compared to the power already unleashed. — No, no, wait, please— it tried, its voice breaking. 81 didn't wait. With a single movement, hardly more than a flick, his nail pierced the dragon's massive eye, bursting it in a geyser of dark, viscous matter that spattered several meters around. An inhuman scream tore through the air, Rex Aira writhing violently in 81's grip, its wings beating frantically, yet unable to free it from that hold. Isidora, phone still in hand, let out a delighted little shriek, instinctively zooming in on the scene. — OH FUCK, she exclaimed, now that's a shot! People are gonna lose their minds! Takeshi abruptly looked away, seized by a violent wave of nausea, one hand pressed against his mouth while the echo of the dragon's scream kept ringing across the white stone expanse. — Is that... is that really necessary? he asked, his voice strangled, not daring to look again. — You asked for his help against a cult, Agent 47 answered soberly, unfazed despite the carnage. This is part of the price. 81, still holding the dying dragon in one hand, finally turned his single eye toward the group, an icy satisfaction crossing his scarred face. — One down, he said, his voice filled with absolute coldness. Nine to go. Rex Aira lay on the ground, its massive body shaken by irregular spasms, its one remaining eye fixed on the empty sky, a trickle of dark blood slowly flowing from its empty socket. Isidora walked up without the slightest embarrassment, crouching near the dying dragon's head, her phone already raised to capture the moment. — Smile for the camera, she said with a little laugh, taking several shots from different angles, completely indifferent to the hoarse moans still escaping the dragon's throat. 81 came over in turn, his heavy steps making the white stone ground vibrate slightly. He drew one of his two swords, the blade sliding out of its sheath with a metallic hiss, and without another word, drove it sharply into Rex Aira's throat. The dragon arched violently one last time, a final hoarse breath escaping its half-open jaws, before falling back, completely still, onto the cracked stone. 81 pulled his blade out with a sharp jerk, the dragon's dark blood dripping along the metal, and put it straight back into its sheath without bothering to wipe it, a reddish trail marking its passage. — That's one, he said simply, his single eye already sweeping the horizon in search of the next. Isidora stood up, putting her phone away after one last satisfied look at her photos. — Okay, she said, we've got the first one. Nine left, like you said. Where are we going now? Agent 47, whose earpiece crackled slightly, turned his head toward the group, his voice still perfectly neutral despite the macabre scene around him. — Reaper has located the four other Archdragons, he said. They are gathered in the same sanctuary, about two kilometers from here. 81 gave a fierce smile, his shoulders straightening, a new impatience running through his massive body. — Perfect, he said. We keep going. Isidora turned her phone back on, a delighted smile on her lips, and switched the app to live mode. — Okay, people, she said, turning the camera on herself as she walked, we're continuing today's little dragon hunt. We just did one, there are four more around here, and I guarantee you this is big stuff. She turned the camera back toward 81, who was walking ahead, his swords still dripping, completely indifferent to the lens aimed at him. — Here's my buddy fresh out of prison, she announced with an almost touristy enthusiasm. Say hi, 81! 81 didn't answer, didn't even slow down, his single eye fixed straight ahead as if the phone, the camera and the millions of potential viewers simply didn't exist. — He's shy, Isidora remarked, unfazed, then turning the lens toward Lucifer, who was walking with perfect nonchalance, apparently already completely used to this kind of situation. — Hi everyone, he said in a monotone voice, giving the camera a vague wave before turning his attention elsewhere, as if it were the most mundane formality in the world. Agent 47 didn't flinch in the slightest when the lens briefly settled on him, simply continuing to walk, his eyes scanning the horizon with total professional concentration, as if the camera were just one more element of the scenery to ignore. Takeshi, on the other hand, froze completely when the phone turned toward him, his eyes going wide. — Wait, what— no, turn that off, he said, hastily raising a hand in front of his face. You can't just... we're tracking down ancient dragons and you're doing a live for your followers?! — Well, yeah, Isidora answered with disarming naturalness, still filming despite his protests. That's exactly what we're doing. Look, there are already twelve thousand people watching. — This is completely insane, Takeshi muttered, finally turning away from the camera, a mixture of exasperation and total disbelief painted on his face. — Shh, said Isidora, a mischievous smile on her lips, you're going to discourage my fans with that negative attitude. Come on, smile a little, it's not every day you get to witness the death of several legendary dragons live. A faint crackle came through Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's synthetic voice rising with its usual mechanical precision. — Updated information, it announced out loud for the group. Rex Stella is currently absent from the sanctuary. He finished with Rex Stella, his hand resting on the immensity of the King of Dragons' skull, an aura of cosmic energy — the vastest of all — slowly flowing out of the remains to join 81, a shiver of power running through his whole body as he absorbed it completely. — And there we go, he said, savoring the sensation, ten fewer on my list. Well, six, counting the dragons as one. Isidora, still live, filmed the scene with undisguised enthusiasm. — People, you are witnessing a cosmic absorption LIVE, she exclaimed. Like, literally nobody else in the known universe can say they've seen this! Lucifer, standing back, watched the scene with placid calm, not the least bit surprised by the scale of the massacre. — That's about what I expected, he remarked simply, as if he were watching a soccer match whose score he already knew. Agent 47, for his part, stayed focused on his earpiece, listening to the latest data transmitted by Reaper. — Analysis complete, he finally announced. Having analyzed the entire fight, I can confirm that even without Isidora's intervention, Rex Stella's chances of survival were zero. Even lower than statistical nothingness. Takeshi, still sitting on the cold stone, looked up at 81, whose body seemed almost to radiate a new power, denser, even more crushing than the one he was already displaying. — So basically, he said, you were just playing with him the whole time. 81 turned his head toward him, a fierce smile stretching across his scarred face, his six hundred and twenty-one hearts now beating with renewed power. — A little, yeah, he admitted. But hey, I had to warm up at least a bit after millennia of sitting still. A faint crackle sounded in Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's synthetic voice speaking up again with its usual precision. — Analysis complete, it announced. Justice Man is currently located on Earth, within KJ's sphere of influence. Current activity: arresting small-time criminals. Isidora, still live, burst out laughing, turning her camera toward 47 to capture his reaction. — Wait, seriously? she said. The guy has a power that can lock anyone up in an infinite dimensional prison, and he spends his time nabbing petty street-corner dealers? — Data confirmed, 47 answered without the slightest trace of irony. 81, who was calmly sheathing his swords, let out an amused rumble. — That's just like him, he remarked. Always wanting to save the world, one jerk at a time. Even when he could take on bigger things. — It's not even ironic, Lucifer added with a crooked smile. That's literally his philosophy. Justice, even on a small scale, matters to him as much as on a big one. Takeshi, finally getting to his feet, brushed off the white dust clinging to his clothes, a mixture of fatigue and apprehension crossing his face. — So where do we go now? he asked. Back to Earth to take him on directly? 81 turned to him, a calculating smile gradually replacing his satisfied look. — Yeah, he said. But this time, we'll have to do it more discreetly. Justice Man, unlike the dragons, isn't the type to get distracted by roasts or Instagram lives. — A real killjoy, then, Isidora remarked, reluctantly putting her phone away at last. Okay, come on, off to Earth then. Agent 47 adjusted his weapon, his gaze already turning toward the horizon, ready to lead the way. — Coordinates transmitted, he said. Ship approaching in three minutes.

codex-t1-c2.title: Chapter 2 — Running from Poppy
codex-t1-c2.html:
The hours slipped by without Takeshi really noticing, the library sunk in a studious silence broken only by the rustle of the pages he turned one after another, more and more feverishly. He had combed through book after book, frantically searching for the slightest mention of talismans, protective seals, rituals capable of driving off an entity like Poppy. He found dozens of references to generic protections — against wandering spirits, against minor curses, against low-ranking demons — but nothing, absolutely nothing, that looked like it could stand up to a creature capable of absorbing its victims after hunting them through their own dreams.

He went back to the book on Alastor, leafing through it page by page again, hoping to find some detail he had missed the first time — a weakness, a method, anything. But the text remained stubbornly silent on that point, merely describing the demon's power and the origin of his creation of Poppy without ever offering the slightest concrete lead on how to protect oneself from her.

It was while closing the book, frustrated, his eyes tired from hours of nonstop reading, that an idea took root in his mind — an idea he knew, the moment it formed, to be both stupid and dangerous. But in his growing despair, it suddenly seemed like the only option he had left.

— Sir, said Takeshi, looking up at the old man a little farther off, busy methodically shelving other books.

The old man turned around, one eyebrow slightly raised at the hesitant tone of his voice.

— What if I summoned Alastor, Takeshi went on, her creator? Do you think he could protect me, with some kind of pact?

The old man stood completely still for a moment, his face freezing into an expression Takeshi couldn't read at first — before understanding, with a slight unease, that it was the look you give someone already condemned.

— You're completely out of your mind, the old man said, his voice steady but charged with a new, almost alarmed intensity. Summoning an overwhelmingly powerful demon to protect yourself from another overwhelmingly powerful entity — if Poppy doesn't kill you, Alastor will. If you do it, do it far from here. But believe me, young man, find another solution.

He came over to the table, planting his cane firmly against the wood, his gaze locked straight onto Takeshi's with a gravity that left no room for doubt.

— You don't understand what you're proposing, he added more quietly, almost like a personal warning. A pact with an entity of that level is never free. Even if, by some miracle, Alastor agreed to protect you, the price he'd demand in return could very well be worse than anything Poppy could do to you. Those creatures don't know mercy. They know self-interest, power, and payment.

Takeshi stayed silent for a long moment, the weight of that warning settling heavily inside him, his fragile determination wavering in the face of the old man's obvious gravity. But deep down, one thought persisted, stubborn, refusing to leave him entirely: for now, he had absolutely no other option on the table — only partial, uncertain protections, and the terrifying wait for his next sleep, when Poppy, this time, might no longer come to play.

— I understand the risk, he said finally, his voice low but firm. But if I do nothing, she'll kill me anyway. At least with a pact, I might have a chance.

The old man looked at him for a long time, a mixture of sadness and resignation crossing his age-lined features, before slowly shaking his head.

— Then I can't stop you, he said at last, his voice softer, almost fatherly despite the gravity of the situation. But if you're really set on doing this, whatever you do, don't do it here. And pray that the demon you summon still has, somewhere inside him, a little of what one might call restraint.

Takeshi left the library late in the afternoon, the book pressed against his chest under his jacket, the old man's grave look still hooked into his mind like an extra weight. He got back in his car and drove, not home this time, but toward a forest he had spotted on the way, a few kilometers farther on, dense and isolated enough that he was sure not to run into anyone.

He parked on a barely visible dirt track, cut the engine and sat still for a moment, hands clenched on the wheel, feeling his heart beat harder as the moment drew near. Then he got out, the book under his arm, and plunged in among the trees, branches cracking under his feet, the daylight already fading through the thick foliage.

He found a small clearing, open enough, surrounded by trees thick enough to create an almost total sense of isolation. The silence there was different from the library's — more alive, punctuated by the distant rustle of wind in the branches and the occasional song of an invisible bird, and yet just as oppressive in its own way.

He knelt in the center of the clearing, set the book down open in front of him at the right page, and picked up a flat stone from the ground, its surface hard and sharp enough to trace clean lines in the soft earth.

His hands trembled slightly as he began to draw, reproducing with the greatest care the complex pentagram illustrated in the book — lines crisscrossing in a precise pattern, dotted with strange symbols whose meaning he didn't understand but which he copied scrupulously, checking every detail against the original illustration several times. The work took him long minutes, sweat beading on his forehead despite the rising evening chill, his knees sinking slightly into the damp earth.

When he had finally finished, he straightened up a little, contemplating the result with a mixture of apprehension and fragile determination. The pentagram seemed almost alive in the fading light, its lines traced in the earth looking, for a moment, deeper and darker than the simple pressure of a stone should have made them.

He picked the book back up, his eyes running one last time over the text of the summoning, his lips silently forming the foreign syllables to make sure of their pronunciation before actually starting. Then, taking a deep breath, feeling his pulse hammer against his temples, he raised his eyes to the pentagram and began to speak, his voice echoing strangely in the deepening silence of the clearing.

— Великий демон из самых глубин ада, услышь мой зов, приди к моей нечистой душе и внемли мне.

The words left his lips with a gravity he hadn't known he was capable of, each syllable seeming to weigh more than the last, as if the very air around him grew denser as he spoke. The wind, which had been rustling softly in the branches a few moments earlier, suddenly seemed to hold its breath. The birds fell silent all at once, a total, unnatural silence crashing down over the whole clearing.

The pentagram traced in the earth began to glow faintly, a dark, reddish light seeping slowly along its complex lines, pulsing like a heart waking after a long slumber.

Takeshi stayed frozen, the book still clutched in his trembling hands, his eyes riveted on that growing light, while a new smell began to fill the air around him — something between heated metal and sulfur, a smell he knew all too well since that terrifying night in his own apartment.

The ground itself seemed to vibrate imperceptibly beneath his knees, and at the center of the pentagram, the shadow began to thicken, to grow denser, gradually taking on a shape that had nothing natural about it — a silhouette slowly forming in the deepening darkness, motionless, patient, as if it had been waiting for this call for far longer than the few seconds the summoning had just taken.

The ground at the center of the pentagram split open suddenly, a dark crack opening without the slightest sound of displaced earth, as if the matter itself were stepping aside out of pure obedience rather than physical force. No body came out of that fissure, no figure of flesh — only a shadow, dense and perfectly black, rising slowly from the opening like thick smoke stubbornly refusing to dissipate.

It unfurled above the pentagram, taking on a vaguely humanoid shape without ever fully solidifying, its outline rippling slightly as if it existed straddling several states of matter at once. Two points even darker than the rest of its mass seemed to serve as eyes, fixed directly on Takeshi with a chilling intensity.

— Who dared disturb me during my 47th murder of the day? a deep, composed voice rang out from that mass of shadow, each word seeming to form without any visible mouth uttering a sound, the very air vibrating under the weight of the question.

Takeshi stayed frozen on the ground, unable to move, his breath cut off by the pure terror that had just seized him. The wind was still completely gone, the birds still silent, as if the entire forest were holding its breath before this presence that had just materialized at its heart.

The shadow tilted what seemed to be its head slightly, its outline flickering in the deepening gloom of the clearing, its attention fixed entirely on the young man kneeling before it, still too terrified to say a single word.

Takeshi gathered what little courage he had left, his shaking legs barely holding him in a kneeling position, and bowed his head before the mass of shadow still floating above the pentagram, its outline still unstable, almost hypnotic in its perpetual motion.

— Great demon Alastor, please grant me your mercy and fulfill my request, he said, his voice trembling but carried by a desperate determination. Help me protect myself from Poppy, your creation.

A heavy silence followed those words, the shadow remaining perfectly still for a long moment, as if it took an almost cruel pleasure in leaving Takeshi to stew in uncertainty. Then, without warning, a kind of low, grating laugh rose from the dark mass, a sound with absolutely nothing human in its texture, echoing against the surrounding trees with an almost physical depth.

— No dice, buddy, said the voice, amused contempt clearly piercing through every syllable. You really thought I'd save a human just for the hell of it? What, were you dropped on your head as a baby?

Takeshi felt his stomach knot even tighter, panic threatening to overwhelm him completely in the face of such an immediate, contemptuous rejection. But he immediately thought of Poppy's voice, of that promise of certain death if he ever failed to find a solution, and that thought alone was enough to rekindle, at the very last moment, his wavering determination.

— I'll offer you whatever you want in exchange, he said hastily, his words almost tumbling over each other, his hands nervously gripping the edge of the book still lying in front of him.

The shadow stayed silent a moment, its outline tightening slightly, as if this offer had finally awakened a hint of genuine interest behind the mocking indifference it had shown so far.

— Fine, the voice said at last, slower this time, almost savoring each word. I'm willing to take you somewhere Poppy can't go. But you're not gonna like it, little human.

An icy shiver ran down Takeshi's spine, the fragile satisfaction of getting a positive answer quickly replaced by a new apprehension, duller still than the one he already felt — the vague certainty that this demon, whatever he truly was behind that shifting mass of shadow, was probably offering him nothing that would resemble, even remotely, real relief.

The shadow spread out a little further, as if to give even more weight to what it was about to say, its flickering outline casting moving shadows all around the already darkening clearing.

— I can take your soul to Hell, the voice said, an almost theatrical calm piercing through every word. But the price to pay will be your death, since a soul can only go to Hell if it's dead. Poppy won't find you there. And trust me, getting caught by Poppy is worse than going to Hell, so make your choice fast, damn it, I've got stuff to do, you know, being the Devil's second-in-command, or Lulu's, call him whatever you want.

Takeshi stayed silent for a long moment, kneeling in the cold earth, the terrible weight of this offer crashing down on him with a brutality he hadn't anticipated. To die. That was the price. Not protection, not a reprieve — his own death, offered in exchange for some semblance of safety in a place he knew absolutely nothing about, except that a demon himself described it as worse than the creature already hunting him.

His mind began to spin in circles, bringing back, against his will, images he would rather never have relived — the blue fire of his recurring nightmare, his father's hand letting go of his for the last time, the old man in the library's grave look warning him against exactly this kind of rushed decision. He thought of his mother, of his girlfriend, of the ordinary life he had still been living just a few days earlier, before everything tipped over into this spiral of terror with no way out in sight.

But he immediately thought again of Poppy's voice echoing in the emptiness of his own apartment, of that icy promise that next time she wouldn't come just to play. He thought again of the old man's words, of that near-unanimous certainty that no one, ever, had truly escaped this kind of entity once it had chosen its prey.

Between a delayed, uncertain death, preceded by an endless, terrifying hunt — and an immediate death, but one that would at least offer him, perhaps, some semblance of respite far from Poppy — the choice, horrible as it was, began to seem less and less absurd.

He closed his eyes for a moment, one last image of his mother on the phone, of his girlfriend telling him she would always be there to listen, crossing his mind with a dull, tearing pain. Then he opened his eyes again, his gaze rising to the mass of shadow still hanging above the pentagram, and slowly nodded, his voice trembling but determined when he finally spoke.

— I accept.

The shadow seemed almost to come alive with a new enthusiasm, its outline tightening slightly around a shape that recalled, for an instant, a smile far too wide for any normal face.

— Alright then, how do you want to die? asked Alastor, his voice drawling with an almost cheerful lightness, completely disconnected from the gravity of the moment. Axe to the head, torture, heart attack, crushed by a rock maybe?

Takeshi swallowed painfully, his whole body now trembling beyond his control, but his voice still managed to come out, firmer than he would have thought possible.

— I want a quick death, he said, and a painless one.

— Well, heart attack it is, then, Alastor answered with an almost disappointing casualness, as if the request sorely lacked originality in his eyes.

A shape detached itself from the main mass of shadow, stretching slowly toward Takeshi, vaguely taking on the appearance of a hand with fingers too long and too thin to belong to anything human. Takeshi didn't move, didn't back away, his eyes fixed on that hand of shadow inexorably approaching his chest, one last fleeting thought for his mother, for his girlfriend, crossing his mind before contact was made.

He felt the shadow touch his heart — a cold and strangely precise sensation, passing straight through his flesh and bones as if they simply didn't exist, reaching the organ itself with terrifying ease.

Then, without the slightest further warning, the pain exploded.

A blinding, absolute flash, a crushing pressure at the center of his chest, as if his heart itself were collapsing in on itself in a fraction of a second. Takeshi didn't even have time to scream — his body arched violently, his eyes widening with the shock, before everything stopped dead.

His body slumped limply onto the pentagram traced in the earth, now completely still, while the reddish glow surrounding it slowly began to fade. Alastor's shadow hung for a moment above the remains, its flickering outline observing the result of its work with an almost clinical indifference, before leaning slightly toward what was left of Takeshi, now ready, one way or another, to make the journey to a place he still knew nothing about.

A blurry, painful consciousness slowly returned to Takeshi, as if he were rising to the surface after an endless drowning. The first thing he noticed was the smell — acrid, thick, a mixture of sulfur, dried blood and something burned he couldn't quite identify. The second was the light, a diffuse reddish hue that seemed to come from everywhere at once, with no precise source, tinting every surface with a sickly glow.

He opened his eyes with difficulty, a total disorientation seizing him as he tried to understand where he was. His back was resting against something hard and uneven, and when he painfully tried to sit up, he felt a texture under his hands that froze him in horror.

Bones.

He was lying in the middle of a veritable heap of bones, some old and bleached, others still covered in strips of dried flesh, forming a kind of macabre hill that stretched for several meters around him. He scrambled to his feet, a shudder of mingled disgust and terror running through him, his feet clumsily searching for stable footing in the middle of this mass grave.

That was when he saw him.

Alastor was sitting a little farther off, on a makeshift throne made of a pile of skulls, one leg crossed nonchalantly over the other. But this time, he was no longer just a shapeless shadow. A very real body sat there — tall, slender, dressed in dark, old-fashioned clothes, a wide smile permanently frozen on a face with fine, almost elegant features, in violent contrast with the macabre scene around him.

He was casually holding a torn-off head between his hands, spinning it with an almost childish gesture, the way a kid would play with a ball, his fingers sometimes sinking into the empty eye sockets with a wet sound that made Takeshi nauseous. He seemed completely absorbed in this morbid pastime — until his eyes lifted, precisely at the moment Takeshi fully regained consciousness, as if he had been waiting for this awakening with the calm patience of someone who knew exactly when it would happen.

— Ah, there you are, finally awake, said Alastor, his voice now far clearer, more embodied than the shadowy rumble it had been in the clearing, but just as loaded with that same contemptuous nonchalance. I was starting to wonder if you were gonna sleep much longer.

He carelessly tossed the head he was holding onto the surrounding pile of bones, where it rolled silently to a stop against a femur, before getting up from his makeshift throne, dusting his hands off against each other as if ridding himself of a bit of dust rather than human remains.

— Welcome to Hell, little human, he added, his arms spreading slightly in a theatrical gesture taking in the whole glowing red expanse around them. I hope for your sake you don't have high expectations, because this isn't really the kind of place that disappoints in a good way.

Takeshi stood frozen, his legs wobbling, his eyes frantically sweeping the reddish horizon stretching as far as the eye could see — dark, tortured structures standing out in the distance, faraway screams carried on a hot, dry wind, and that omnipresent red light that seemed to tint the very air with a permanent threat.

He was dead. He was really dead, and he was now standing, very real in spite of everything, in the very heart of Hell — facing a demon who had literally crushed his heart a few moments earlier, and who was now looking at him with the amused, perfectly detached expression of someone eyeing a freshly unwrapped toy.

Not protection, not a reprieve — his own death, offered in exchange for some semblance of safety in a place he knew absolutely nothing about, except that a demon himself described it as worse than the creature already hunting him. His mind began to spin in circles, bringing back, against his will, images he would rather never have relived — the blue fire of his recurring nightmare, his father's hand letting go of his for the last time, the old man in the library's grave look warning him against exactly this kind of rushed decision. He thought of his mother, of his girlfriend, of the ordinary life he had still been living just a few days earlier, before everything tipped over into this spiral of terror with no way out in sight. But he immediately thought again of Poppy's voice echoing in the emptiness of his own apartment, of that icy promise that next time she wouldn't come just to play. He thought again of the old man's words, of that near-unanimous certainty that no one, ever, had truly escaped this kind of entity once it had chosen its prey. Between a delayed, uncertain death, preceded by an endless, terrifying hunt — and an immediate death, but one that would at least offer him, perhaps, some semblance of respite far from Poppy — the choice, horrible as it was, began to seem less and less absurd. He closed his eyes for a moment, one last image of his mother on the phone, of his girlfriend telling him she would always be there to listen, crossing his mind with a dull, tearing pain. Then he opened his eyes again, his gaze rising to the mass of shadow still hanging above the pentagram, and slowly nodded, his voice trembling but determined when he finally spoke. — I accept. The shadow seemed almost to come alive with a new enthusiasm, its outline tightening slightly around a shape that recalled, for an instant, a smile far too wide for any normal face. — Alright then, how do you want to die? asked Alastor, his voice drawling with an almost cheerful lightness, completely disconnected from the gravity of the moment. Axe to the head, torture, heart attack, crushed by a rock maybe? Takeshi swallowed painfully, his whole body now trembling beyond his control, but his voice still managed to come out, firmer than he would have thought possible. — I want a quick death, he said, and a painless one. — Well, heart attack it is, then, Alastor answered with an almost disappointing casualness, as if the request sorely lacked originality in his eyes. A shape detached itself from the main mass of shadow, stretching slowly toward Takeshi, vaguely taking on the appearance of a hand with fingers too long and too thin to belong to anything human. Takeshi didn't move, didn't back away, his eyes fixed on that hand of shadow inexorably approaching his chest, one last fleeting thought for his mother, for his girlfriend, crossing his mind before contact was made. He felt the shadow touch his heart — a cold and strangely precise sensation, passing straight through his flesh and bones as if they simply didn't exist, reaching the organ itself with terrifying ease. Then, without the slightest further warning, the pain exploded. A blinding, absolute flash, a crushing pressure at the center of his chest, as if his heart itself were collapsing in on itself in a fraction of a second. Takeshi didn't even have time to scream — his body arched violently, his eyes widening with the shock, before everything stopped dead. His body slumped limply onto the pentagram traced in the earth, now completely still, while the reddish glow surrounding it slowly began to fade. Alastor's shadow hung for a moment above the remains, its flickering outline observing the result of its work with an almost clinical indifference, before leaning slightly toward what was left of Takeshi, now ready, one way or another, to make the journey to a place he still knew nothing about. A blurry, painful consciousness slowly returned to Takeshi, as if he were rising to the surface after an endless drowning. The first thing he noticed was the smell — acrid, thick, a mixture of sulfur, dried blood and something burned he couldn't quite identify. The second was the light, a diffuse reddish hue that seemed to come from everywhere at once, with no precise source, tinting every surface with a sickly glow. He opened his eyes with difficulty, a total disorientation seizing him as he tried to understand where he was. His back was resting against something hard and uneven, and when he painfully tried to sit up, he felt a texture under his hands that froze him in horror. Bones. He was lying in the middle of a veritable heap of bones, some old and bleached, others still covered in strips of dried flesh, forming a kind of macabre hill that stretched for several meters around him. He scrambled to his feet, a shudder of mingled disgust and terror running through him, his feet clumsily searching for stable footing in the middle of this mass grave. That was when he saw him. Alastor was sitting a little farther off, on a makeshift throne made of a pile of skulls, one leg crossed nonchalantly over the other. But this time, he was no longer just a shapeless shadow. A very real body sat there — tall, slender, dressed in dark, old-fashioned clothes, a wide smile permanently frozen on a face with fine, almost elegant features, in violent contrast with the macabre scene around him. He was casually holding a torn-off head between his hands, spinning it with an almost childish gesture, the way a kid would play with a ball, his fingers sometimes sinking into the empty eye sockets with a wet sound that made Takeshi nauseous. He seemed completely absorbed in this morbid pastime — until his eyes lifted, precisely at the moment Takeshi fully regained consciousness, as if he had been waiting for this awakening with the calm patience of someone who knew exactly when it would happen. — Ah, there you are, finally awake, said Alastor, his voice now far clearer, more embodied than the shadowy rumble it had been in the clearing, but just as loaded with that same contemptuous nonchalance. I was starting to wonder if you were gonna sleep much longer. He carelessly tossed the head he was holding onto the surrounding pile of bones, where it rolled silently to a stop against a femur, before getting up from his makeshift throne, dusting his hands off against each other as if ridding himself of a bit of dust rather than human remains. — Welcome to Hell, little human, he added, his arms spreading slightly in a theatrical gesture taking in the whole glowing red expanse around them. I hope for your sake you don't have high expectations, because this isn't really the kind of place that disappoints in a good way. Takeshi stood frozen, his legs wobbling, his eyes frantically sweeping the reddish horizon stretching as far as the eye could see — dark, tortured structures standing out in the distance, faraway screams carried on a hot, dry wind, and that omnipresent red light that seemed to tint the very air with a permanent threat. He was dead. He was really dead, and he was now standing, very real in spite of everything, in the very heart of Hell — facing a demon who had literally crushed his heart a few moments earlier, and who was now looking at him with the amused, perfectly detached expression of someone eyeing a freshly unwrapped toy.

codex-t1-c3.title: Chapter 3 — A Guided Tour of Hell
codex-t1-c3.html:
Takeshi stood still for a long moment, his eyes riveted on the reddish horizon, unable to tear his gaze from those tortured structures rising in the distance like the bones of a fossilized giant. Every breath he took burned his throat slightly, the hot, dry air heavy with a smell of sulfur that seemed to seep straight into his lungs.

— Right, said Alastor, stretching with an almost comical nonchalance, since you're stuck here for a good while, I might as well give you the grand tour. I don't have much else to do today, and honestly, it's been ages since I had a tourist to torment with useless explanations.

He came down from the pile of bones with surprising agility, his steps making almost no sound despite the ground littered with bone fragments, and waved Takeshi over with his hand, the way you'd call a stubborn dog.

— Come on, move it, he added. Dead people who dawdle get on my nerves.

Takeshi hesitated a second, his legs still shaking, before resigning himself to obey — what other option did he have anyway, dead and on his own in a place he knew absolutely nothing about? He climbed down the hill of bones in turn, nearly tripping several times, and caught up with Alastor, who had already started strolling off toward what looked, in the distance, like an entire city carved out of black rock.

— Where are we exactly? Takeshi asked, his voice still hesitant, his dry throat making every word hard to get out.

— In my private garden, technically, Alastor answered with an even wider smile, waving vaguely at the mass grave they had just left. That's where I bring the ones I... how to put it... finish off personally. It's a tradition.

Takeshi felt his stomach turn and preferred not to push the subject any further. They walked in silence for several minutes, the landscape gradually changing around them — rocky plains dotted with smoking crevasses slowly gave way to more organized structures, paths carved into the rock, then finally the first silhouettes of buildings standing out against the glowing sky.

The city itself turned out to be vaster and more complex than anything Takeshi could have imagined. Tortured towers rose toward a starless sky, their facades carved with screaming faces frozen in the black stone. Suspension bridges connected some of the buildings, spanning chasms from which unsettling orange glows escaped. And everywhere, figures were moving — some humanoid but deformed, others almost completely unrecognizable, sporting horns, tails, leathery wings stretched across their backs.

— What... what is all this? Takeshi asked, his voice betraying both horror and a fascination he couldn't help.

— The capital, Alastor said with sarcastic pride. Well, one of the capitals. Hell is big, you know, we didn't do things halfway. This is the heart of power — Lucifer's palace is right over there, he added, pointing to a massive structure in the distance, its towers so tall they seemed to pierce the red sky itself.

Takeshi followed his gaze, glimpsing the imposing silhouette of the palace, its dark walls adorned with flames that seemed to dance along its facades without ever going out.

— Lucifer, he repeated softly, the name echoing in him with a weight he didn't really understand, just a vague impression, drawn from his memories of pop culture, that this was someone you'd be better off never meeting.

— Yep, the king himself, Alastor confirmed, setting off toward the city again. Don't worry, you won't run into him today, I'm not planning to drag you all the way to his throne. He's got other things on his mind right now.

They headed into the narrow streets of the city, where the bustle contrasted strangely with the oppressive atmosphere of the place. Makeshift markets sprawled along some of the alleys, creatures trading what looked like miniature souls trapped in glass vials for other equally strange goods. Screams sometimes rang out in the distance, mixed with laughter that had nothing human about it, and Takeshi caught himself instinctively sticking closer to Alastor, despite the visceral terror he still felt toward him.

— Why is everyone scared of you? he finally asked, noticing the way every creature they passed hurriedly stepped aside, some going so far as to lower their eyes to the ground.

Alastor gave a short laugh, dry and amused, without even slowing down.

— Because I'm the Devil's Second, he said with an obvious hint of pride. The second most powerful demon in all of this Hell. And because I have the nasty habit of ripping off the heads of people who annoy me a little too quickly. You're starting to get the picture, I hope.

Takeshi nodded, his throat tightening even more at the reminder, his steps becoming a little more careful despite himself.

They kept going through several districts, Alastor commenting on each place with an almost offhand detachment — a building used as a prison where souls screamed without pause, an arena where fights to the death went on nonstop purely for the entertainment of the demons watching, a central square where an immense statue depicted, in Alastor's words, "a former king of Hell, who died in circumstances best not mentioned too loudly."

They finally stopped at the top of a small hill overlooking part of the city, offering a sweeping view of the glowing expanse stretching as far as the eye could see, dotted with flames and thick smoke rising toward a sky still deprived of stars.

— So, said Alastor, finally turning toward him with that smile, as wide and unsettling as ever. What do you think of your new home?

Takeshi stayed silent for a long moment, contemplating the infernal landscape stretching out before him, this crushing reality that had just overturned absolutely everything he thought he knew about existence itself. The fear was still there, lurking deep inside him, but something else was starting to emerge too — a kind of cautious resignation, almost a survival instinct whispering to him that from now on, he'd be better off learning to navigate this world than continuing to passively endure it.

— It's... a lot to take in, he said finally, his voice steadier than he would have thought possible.

— That's for sure, Alastor agreed with a satisfied little laugh. Don't worry, little human, you'll get used to it. Or not. Honestly, that's not really my business, as long as you don't bug me more than necessary.

He set off again, strolling back down the hill, leaving Takeshi to follow him in silence, his gaze lingering one last time on the glowing immensity of Hell spreading all around him — this open-air prison where he would now have to learn to survive, far from Poppy, but also far, for good, from everything he had known until now.

They resumed their walk through the winding streets of the city, Alastor pointing out in passing a building livelier than the others, from which guttural laughter and a discordant music with nothing human in its rhythm spilled out.

— That's a bar, he said, gesturing vaguely at the place. If you ever get bored, you can always go drink something there that'll make you regret ever being born. Well, dying. Or else, he added with an even wider smile, you can go get into a fight in the street, if you feel like stretching your legs. Here, the law only exists when the king decides to deal with something personally, which, believe me, doesn't happen often. The rest of the time, it's every man for himself.

Takeshi cast an uncertain glance at the bar, then at the surrounding streets, where a few scuffles did indeed seem to be going on without any authority stepping in, shouts and the sound of blows echoing occasionally between the buildings without anyone being particularly bothered.

— Lovely place, he muttered, a fragile sarcasm barely showing through his ever-present terror.

Alastor gave a short laugh, clearly unbothered by the tone of the remark, and kept walking in silence for a while before turning to him again, an unusual glint of interest crossing his eyes.

— Tell me, he asked suddenly, do you know the two masters of the universe, above Hell and every other force in existence?

Takeshi frowned, his mind still too saturated by everything he had just discovered to really grasp the scope of the question.

— No, he answered finally. I didn't even know they existed.

— Well, first we've got KJ and his higher incarnations, Alastor began, his voice taking on an almost professorial tone, tinged with an underlying amusement that never really left him. An entity older than everything that exists, so powerful he could literally erase Hell with a snap of his fingers if he felt like it. And then, he added with an even wider smile, we've got 81, the God Killer.

He paused for a moment, as if to let the weight of that name settle properly before going on, and Takeshi felt a familiar shiver run down his spine — that same name he had already come across without knowing it in the pages of the library book, mixed in with the mysteries of Alastor himself.

— He was human, originally, Alastor went on, his voice momentarily losing its usual lightness for a calmer, almost respectful tone. His mother fell seriously ill, he prayed to the gods to save her, and they did nothing. Total silence. His mother died, and him, instead of just crying in his corner like any normal human, he decided to go kill the god of his own religion. And he didn't stop there.

He started walking again, Takeshi following obediently, his attention now completely absorbed by the story.

— For a billion years, Alastor continued, he hunted the gods, one by one, absorbing their power and their soul with every kill. Eighty-one gods a day, on average — hence the name. He became so powerful that he ended up surpassing the gods themselves, plain and simple. He even destroyed Heaven at one point, which, believe me, is no small feat.

Takeshi stayed silent, trying as best he could to take in the scale of what he had just heard, this level of power and violence that completely exceeded anything he could have imagined possible just a few days earlier.

— Ten of us finally joined forces to seal him away, Alastor added, a darker gleam briefly crossing his eyes. Me included, indirectly — well, not me personally, but people at my level of power, you get the idea. We never managed to kill him, mind you. We only managed to hold him back. For now.

He glanced with amusement at Takeshi, whose face had grown paler with each new detail of the story.

— There you go, little human, he concluded with a satisfied smile. Now you have a better idea of what kind of universe you've just landed in. It's a lot bigger, and a lot scarier, than your little dockworker life on Earth.

— Right, said Alastor after a moment of silence, stretching with that nonchalance that never seemed to leave him. Feel like going to see Lucifer? Just to show you a bit higher up the ladder, while we're at it.

Takeshi hesitated, a shiver of apprehension immediately running down his spine at the mere mention of that name, which he was only just beginning to associate in his mind with a power far beyond anything he had imagined so far. But he glanced quickly around him, at the streets where fights were still breaking out sporadically, at the creatures that systematically stepped aside as soon as Alastor approached — and he understood, with an almost desperate clarity, that staying away from him would probably mean signing his own death warrant far faster than any visit to the palace.

— Okay, he said finally, his voice hesitant but resigned.

They went on their way, crossing more suspension bridges over smoking chasms, walking along streets where the bustle never really seemed to stop — screams, laughter, sounds of struggle blending into a chaotic background noise Takeshi was beginning, despite himself, to get somewhat used to. He stayed close to Alastor the whole time, his presence becoming, against all odds, a strange kind of safety in the middle of a world that seemed to want to crush him around every corner.

The palace finally rose before them, even more imposing up close than Takeshi had guessed from the hill. Its black walls, carved with eternal flames, rose toward a sky still deprived of stars, and two massive guards, half human and half beast in appearance, stood on either side of a monumental door.

— Good day, Master Alastor, welcome to the Palace, said one of the guards, bowing slightly, his gravelly voice full of obvious respect, immediately stepping aside to let him through.

Alastor walked on without even slowing down, but stopped almost at once when he noticed that Takeshi, one step behind, had just been blocked by the second guard, a spear crossed in front of him to bar his way.

— You are not authorized to enter, new soul, the guard said curtly, his suspicious eyes sweeping Takeshi from head to toe.

Alastor slowly turned around, his smile widening in a way that boded nothing good, a cold gleam crossing his usually mocking eyes.

— He's with me, he said in a calm voice, but one carrying an undeniable weight. Let him through, unless my orders don't suit you — in which case, we can discuss it.

The guard froze instantly, a sudden, visible fear crossing his bestial features, his spear hastily pulling back as he bowed in turn, almost despite himself, in a reflex of immediate submission.

— No, no, go ahead, young soul, he stammered, quickly stepping aside to clear the way, his shifting eyes carefully avoiding Alastor's.

Takeshi stepped forward cautiously, his heart still pounding, but with a hint of relief at seeing, once again, how Alastor's mere implicit threat was enough to bend any resistance in his path. He gave the two guards, already back in position, one last look, their tense expressions clearly betraying their relief at seeing them go without incident, before following Alastor through the great doors of the palace, sinking even deeper into this world that kept, with every step, completely redefining the limits of what he thought was possible.

Takeshi watched, fascinated despite himself, how every demon they passed on the palace's upper floors literally froze as they went by. The higher they climbed, the more powerful the creatures they met seemed — their silhouettes more massive, their auras heavier, some giving off a heat or a cold you could feel even from a distance — and yet none of them dared so much as turn their head toward Alastor. Some looked away outright, staring at the floor or a wall with almost painful concentration. Others were visibly holding their breath, their chests motionless, as if the very air around Alastor had become territory better left undisturbed.

— Do you always have this effect? Takeshi asked, his voice low, almost a whisper, as if he were afraid of breaking that oppressive silence himself.

— Of course, Alastor answered without slowing down, a satisfied smile spreading slightly across his lips. These inferior beings are afraid. Their survival instinct kicks in. They know that getting close to me would mean certain death — and even if they probably want to kill me, or put me through fates worse than death, he said, still climbing the palace floors, they also know they don't have the slightest means to do it. So they keep quiet. They barely breathe. It's safer.

He glanced sideways at Takeshi, his smile widening even more, almost amused by his own reputation.

— You, on the other hand, apparently don't have that instinct, he added. You ask me questions like I'm your drinking buddy. Either it's courage, or you're just too dumb to be scared properly. I still can't tell which.

They passed a wide hallway lined with columns even taller than the previous ones, where two demons — horned creatures with almost translucent skin, dark veins visibly pulsing beneath the surface — stepped aside so abruptly that one of them nearly stumbled into the wall. Neither said a word. Neither looked at them directly. Takeshi simply saw them lower their eyes, jaws clenched, until he and Alastor had disappeared around the next bend in the hallway.

— Do they hate you that much? Takeshi asked, a hint of curiosity piercing through the caution in his voice.

— Hate is a strong word, Alastor answered with a dry little laugh. Let's say they fear me with a very, very bitter admiration. Most of the ones we just passed would love to take my place. Some have even tried, in the past. It never ended very well for them.

He stopped for a moment in front of a massive door engraved with symbols Takeshi didn't recognize, resting his hand on it almost carelessly.

— We're getting close to the throne room, he said, his tone shifting slightly, losing a fragment of its usual lightness. So do me a favor, little human: in there, you keep your mouth shut, unless Lulu speaks to you directly. That's not advice. That's an order.

But he glanced quickly around him, at the streets where fights were still breaking out sporadically, at the creatures that systematically stepped aside as soon as Alastor approached — and he understood, with an almost desperate clarity, that staying away from him would probably mean signing his own death warrant far faster than any visit to the palace. — Okay, he said finally, his voice hesitant but resigned. They went on their way, crossing more suspension bridges over smoking chasms, walking along streets where the bustle never really seemed to stop — screams, laughter, sounds of struggle blending into a chaotic background noise Takeshi was beginning, despite himself, to get somewhat used to. He stayed close to Alastor the whole time, his presence becoming, against all odds, a strange kind of safety in the middle of a world that seemed to want to crush him around every corner. The palace finally rose before them, even more imposing up close than Takeshi had guessed from the hill. Its black walls, carved with eternal flames, rose toward a sky still deprived of stars, and two massive guards, half human and half beast in appearance, stood on either side of a monumental door. — Good day, Master Alastor, welcome to the Palace, said one of the guards, bowing slightly, his gravelly voice full of obvious respect, immediately stepping aside to let him through. Alastor walked on without even slowing down, but stopped almost at once when he noticed that Takeshi, one step behind, had just been blocked by the second guard, a spear crossed in front of him to bar his way. — You are not authorized to enter, new soul, the guard said curtly, his suspicious eyes sweeping Takeshi from head to toe. Alastor slowly turned around, his smile widening in a way that boded nothing good, a cold gleam crossing his usually mocking eyes. — He's with me, he said in a calm voice, but one carrying an undeniable weight. Let him through, unless my orders don't suit you — in which case, we can discuss it. The guard froze instantly, a sudden, visible fear crossing his bestial features, his spear hastily pulling back as he bowed in turn, almost despite himself, in a reflex of immediate submission. — No, no, go ahead, young soul, he stammered, quickly stepping aside to clear the way, his shifting eyes carefully avoiding Alastor's. Takeshi stepped forward cautiously, his heart still pounding, but with a hint of relief at seeing, once again, how Alastor's mere implicit threat was enough to bend any resistance in his path. He gave the two guards, already back in position, one last look, their tense expressions clearly betraying their relief at seeing them go without incident, before following Alastor through the great doors of the palace, sinking even deeper into this world that kept, with every step, completely redefining the limits of what he thought was possible. Takeshi watched, fascinated despite himself, how every demon they passed on the palace's upper floors literally froze as they went by. The higher they climbed, the more powerful the creatures they met seemed — their silhouettes more massive, their auras heavier, some giving off a heat or a cold you could feel even from a distance — and yet none of them dared so much as turn their head toward Alastor. Some looked away outright, staring at the floor or a wall with almost painful concentration. Others were visibly holding their breath, their chests motionless, as if the very air around Alastor had become territory better left undisturbed. — Do you always have this effect? Takeshi asked, his voice low, almost a whisper, as if he were afraid of breaking that oppressive silence himself. — Of course, Alastor answered without slowing down, a satisfied smile spreading slightly across his lips. These inferior beings are afraid. Their survival instinct kicks in. They know that getting close to me would mean certain death — and even if they probably want to kill me, or put me through fates worse than death, he said, still climbing the palace floors, they also know they don't have the slightest means to do it. So they keep quiet. They barely breathe. It's safer. He glanced sideways at Takeshi, his smile widening even more, almost amused by his own reputation. — You, on the other hand, apparently don't have that instinct, he added. You ask me questions like I'm your drinking buddy. Either it's courage, or you're just too dumb to be scared properly. I still can't tell which. They passed a wide hallway lined with columns even taller than the previous ones, where two demons — horned creatures with almost translucent skin, dark veins visibly pulsing beneath the surface — stepped aside so abruptly that one of them nearly stumbled into the wall. Neither said a word. Neither looked at them directly. Takeshi simply saw them lower their eyes, jaws clenched, until he and Alastor had disappeared around the next bend in the hallway. — Do they hate you that much? Takeshi asked, a hint of curiosity piercing through the caution in his voice. — Hate is a strong word, Alastor answered with a dry little laugh. Let's say they fear me with a very, very bitter admiration. Most of the ones we just passed would love to take my place. Some have even tried, in the past. It never ended very well for them. He stopped for a moment in front of a massive door engraved with symbols Takeshi didn't recognize, resting his hand on it almost carelessly. — We're getting close to the throne room, he said, his tone shifting slightly, losing a fragment of its usual lightness. So do me a favor, little human: in there, you keep your mouth shut, unless Lulu speaks to you directly. That's not advice. That's an order.

codex-t1-c4.title: Chapter 4 — The Throne Room
codex-t1-c4.html:
The massive doors opened with a dull rumble, revealing an immense hall whose ceiling was lost somewhere above a rain of hanging flames, motionless, as if frozen between two heartbeats. The throne stood at the far end, carved from black stone veined with red, more massive than anything Takeshi could have imagined.

But it wasn't Lucifer sitting on it.

A woman occupied the throne, one leg carelessly slung over the armrest, wrapped in a black cape whose folds seemed to literally swallow the surrounding light — as if the space immediately around her body stubbornly refused to be lit. She was holding a phone at arm's length, her face bent toward the screen, completely absorbed, not sparing the slightest glance for the opening doors or for their entrance.

Alastor was the first to speak, his voice instantly losing all its usual nonchalance.

— Lady Isidora, he said in a calm, almost cautious tone. What are you doing here?

— Shut up, I'm posting a story, she shot back without even looking up, her thumb still sliding across the screen with almost comical concentration.

She finally tapped something, a faint beep confirming it had gone out, before at last setting the phone down on the armrest of the throne and finally raising her eyes — a dark, almost bottomless gaze that swept over Alastor, then Takeshi, with casual indifference.

— Lulu's gone, she went on, stretching slightly and cracking her neck with an almost feline motion. I was waiting for him, but his throne is shit, goddamn it. Stone to sit on. No wonder he's got a stick up his ass.

Takeshi stood frozen near the entrance, his eyes going from Alastor to this woman with growing incomprehension, vaguely sensing that the name — Isidora — was no ordinary one, that the change of tone in Alastor's own voice said a lot about who she might be.

Isidora turned her eyes back to Takeshi, one eyebrow raised, before waving vaguely at Alastor, her black cape slowly rippling around her as if it had its own gravity.

— Al, she said with a touch of theatrical boredom, tell this soul who I am. Can't be bothered to introduce myself.

Alastor sighed, a short, dry sound, before turning slightly toward Takeshi.

— This is Isidora, he said, the Witch of the Void. I'll spare you her story, but she's working with Lucifer to free someone else. But Lulu will explain that to you, if he feels like it.

Isidora nodded, satisfied, her gaze falling back on Takeshi with a new, sharper interest, as if she were only now really noticing him for the first time. She straightened up slightly on the throne, her other leg joining the first in a more upright, more attentive position.

— What's that, she said, nodding her chin at Takeshi, an ordinary dead guy? Or did you pull another one of your stunts, Al?

— A pact, Alastor answered with affected casualness. He wanted to escape Poppy. I figured it was simpler to kill him and bring him here than to wear myself out negotiating with her.

Isidora let out a short laugh, dry and without much warmth, her eyes still fixed on Takeshi with that same unsettling intensity.

— Poppy, she repeated, almost savoring the name. Now that's a great way to make enemies on both sides at once. You're either very smart or completely stupid, kid.

She let the silence settle for a moment, her gaze still not leaving Takeshi, before picking her phone back up from the armrest, her attention already drifting elsewhere, as if the conversation had used up all the interest she could give it.

Isidora briefly looked up from her phone, a crooked smile hovering on her lips.

— Poppy's actually pretty nice, she said with an almost affectionate nonchalance. Even if when she wants to play, she won't let you go. Sometimes she pulls off some fucking brilliant stunts, that's why I like her.

She sat up completely, slipping her phone into an invisible fold of her cape, and rose from the throne in one fluid, almost disinterested movement.

— Right, since Lulu's not here, I'm out. I'll swing by later.

With one hand, she traced a downward motion, as if tearing an invisible curtain hanging in the air. A dark rift opened in front of her, its jagged edges pulsing with a black light that illuminated nothing around it. Without another glance at Takeshi or Alastor, she strolled into it, the rift closing behind her in total silence, as if it had never existed in that room.

Silence fell over the throne room again, broken only by the faint crackle of the flames hanging from the ceiling. Takeshi stood still for a moment, his eyes still fixed on the spot where the rift had just closed, before turning to Alastor.

— What was that? he finally asked, his voice betraying a mixture of bewilderment and renewed caution.

Alastor shrugged, his eyes still on the now-empty throne, an expression hard to read briefly crossing his features.

— That, he said, was Isidora. Don't worry, little human. With her, you never really get used to it. You survive, and that's already not bad.

The sound of hurried footsteps echoed from one of the side corridors, and a demon appeared in the throne room — smaller than the ones they had passed on the lower floors, grayish skin stretched over a hunched body, two small curved horns sticking out of a bald skull. He rushed to Alastor and knelt before him without the slightest hesitation, his forehead almost touching the polished floor.

— Excuse me, great demon Alastor, he said in a trembling voice, but Lord Morningstar is arriving.

— Very well, Alastor answered in a perfectly detached, almost bored tone. Now, out of my sight.

The demon leapt to his feet, mumbling a string of muddled thanks, and vanished as quickly as he had appeared, disappearing down the corridor he had come from without ever daring to look back.

Takeshi, for his part, stood still, his heart suddenly beating harder at the announcement of this imminent arrival. He glanced quickly around the throne room, as if looking for a place to hide, before thinking better of it, vaguely understanding that there was, in any case, absolutely nowhere to hide from what was coming. His hands tightened unconsciously against his thighs, his throat constricting as he stared at the great doors through which Lucifer, the King of Evil himself, would soon make his entrance.
